newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 1.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media & the Internet and Brand-name Products.
ADVERTISING, MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

MADRID - Canal Satelite Digital, the Canal Plus-backed digital television platform in Spain, says it is filing a complaint with the European Union Competition Commission against Telefonica de Espana, which leads the rival Via Digital platform, over Telefonica's purchase of a 25 percent stake in Antena 3 television station and a controlling stake in its GMA subsidiary.
(Reuter)
PARIS - The Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel (CSA), France's broadcasting regulator, says it launches the process of auditing France's FM band signalled at the start of this year. (Reuter)

PARIS - Canal Plus, the French pay TV group, welcomes a broadcasting law approved by the Italian parliament on Tuesday, saying it will provide a stable environment for pay-TV channel Telepiu and help the development of digital television platform.(Reuter)
PARIS - Fleming Securities said it recommends shares in French television station M6-Metropole TV with a price objective of 810 francs ($130) in a year's time. (Reuter)
LONDON - Yahoo! Europe, an Internet search and navigation company, will increase its advertising rates in September because of strong demand, marketing director Iain Osborne says. (Reuter)

WASHINGTON - The American Society of Composers, Authors, and Publishers (ASCAP) has won the right to collect royalties for home taping of copyright music in Canada, France and Germany, the federal government says. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
LONDON - Vendome Luxury Goods Plc says it agreed to acquire Lancel, the French leather goods group, for an estimated 342 million ($225.6 million) Swiss francs. (Reuter)

LONDON - John McGrath, chief executive of Grand Metropolitan Plc, sounds a note of peace in the tussle with rebel shareholder Bernard Arnault, chairman of French luxury goods company LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton. "I think the solution is calm, sane negotiation," he says. (Reuter)

PARIS - Agribusiness group Eridania Beghin-Say says the European Commission's scientific food committee has approved use of its Actilight product for human consumption. Actilight is based on beet sugar and has properties to stimulate and balance intestinal flora, the company says. (Reuter)

PARIS - Tourists are flocking to France in greater numbers than ever before, with Mickey Mouse's European residence the main attraction by far. France's national tourism federation says business is booming, bolstered by currency trends that have cut the cost of a French holiday for many travellers. (Reuter)

LONDON - Cross-channel train operator Eurostar dismisses a fierce attack by a British minister who accused the company of not doing enough to deter illegal migrants travelling from Paris to London, saying it is not required by law to check passports and travel documents. (Reuter)
